introduction: To locate places on Earth, geographers have drawn imaginary horizontal and vertical lines across the globe. These are called Latitudes and Longitudes. At this beginner level, we will understand the foundational meaning of these lines and the primary axes that divide the Earth.

core_concepts.title: Latitudes (Parallels)
core_concepts.description: These are imaginary horizontal lines drawn from East to West across the globe. They are parallel to each other, meaning they never intersect. The distance between any two latitudes is always constant (approximately 111 km).

core_concepts.title: The Equator (0° Latitude)
core_concepts.description: This is the longest latitude line, running exactly across the middle of the Earth. It divides the planet into two equal halves: the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.

core_concepts.title: Longitudes (Meridians)
core_concepts.description: These are imaginary vertical lines drawn from the North Pole to the South Pole. Unlike latitudes, they are NOT parallel. They are farthest apart at the Equator (111.3 km) and gradually converge until they all meet at the poles.

core_concepts.title: Prime Meridian (0° Longitude)
core_concepts.description: This is the 0° vertical line that passes through the Royal Observatory in 'Greenwich', London. It divides the Earth into the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere. The world's standard time is calculated from this line (Greenwich Mean Time / GMT).

important_entities.name: Total Count of Lines
important_entities.significance: There are 360 longitudes (180° East and 180° West). If we draw latitudes at 1° intervals, there are 179 latitude circles (since the 90° North and 90° South poles are just points, not circles, plus 1 Equator).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common exam question: Latitudes are parallel to each other (distance remains the same everywhere), but Longitudes are NOT parallel. The distance between longitudes shrinks as you move from the Equator toward the poles.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember 'Latitudes' are 'Flat' (horizontal/lying down). Remember 'Longitudes' as 'Long' (vertical/standing up).

exam_strategy_tips: The 0° Latitude (Equator) and the 0° Longitude (Prime Meridian) intersect each other in the 'Atlantic Ocean' (Gulf of Guinea). This is a highly repeated direct factual question.
